// Build-A-Player College Football defensive backs: generated by scripts/cfb/build-dbs.mjs (hand-check in
// scripts/cfb/dbs-hand.mjs), ESPN feeds pulled 2026-11-25. Do not hand-edit; re-run the build.
// Read with data/cfb-players.js (the same row shape and the same scale). Assets: scripts/fetch-cfb-assets.mjs.
//
// ── Who is here ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Every 2026 FBS team (138): CB1, CB2 and S1, {{COUNTS}}.
// Read from ESPN's rosters (position CB / S / FS / SS / DB / NB) and ESPN's 2026 box scores (every completed game
// through Week 13's Tuesday games). Depth inside a slot type is the 2026 snaps proxy: a game's tackles + 3 x PD +
// 4 x INT (x 0.1, plus 0.6 for being on the field), the team's last four games counted twice, plus 0.6 for every game
// ESPN's season feed has him playing without a stat (the corner nobody throws at). ESPN has no games started.
// A man out of his team's last four box scores is left out unless he is known to be due back; a season-ending injury
// drops him (below). Nickel/STAR backs are corners here (the contract); Air Force's SPUR and Oklahoma's Cheetah are safeties.
// Corner or safety: ESPN lists 47 teams' backs (and some backs on 30 more) only as "DB". Those were placed from team
//   previews, depth charts and beat coverage found by web search (scratch pos-web.txt); a "DB" nobody's coverage placed
//   takes his stat profile (a logistic fit on the 773 ESPN-labeled CB/S with 4+ weighted games: weight, height,
//   tackles a game, PD share of his plays, INT per PD; right 78% of the time, 91-96% at the ends). Every row's source
//   is in the build's --report.
// Bio (number, height, weight, class, position) and photo: ESPN. espn = the ESPN athlete id. espnPos = ESPN's listing.
// year: ESPN's roster class, with RS- when his FBS lines show a season of 4 games or fewer since his class says he
//   enrolled (or FBS games before that year) and he has a 5-game FBS season on record. Approximate, as the offense
//   pools: ESPN has no redshirt field and FCS/JUCO years are invisible to these feeds.
// s26 / s25: his 2026 (to date) and 2025 FBS lines from ESPN's box scores (bowls included), g = ESPN's games played
//   (the season feed; a man appears in a box score only with a stat), ff = forced fumbles from ESPN's season feed
//   (regular season; the box scores have none). pd = passes broken up (ESPN's PD, which leaves out interceptions),
//   td = defensive touchdowns (INT returns included), intTd = the INT-return ones.
// skin: the median skin-coloured pixel of his ESPN headshot's face box, null without a photo.
//
// ── Grade scale (the NFL 0-11 scale, read against college players, as data/cfb-players.js) ────────────────────
//   0 F · 1 D · 2 C- · 3 C · 4 C+ · 5 B- · 6 B · 7 B+ · 8 A- · 9 A · 10 A+ · 11 S
//   Checked on the output:
{{CHECKS}}
//   The offense pools on the same check: P4 starters QB 6.7 / WR 6.8 / RB 6.3 · G6 starters QB 5.9 / WR 5.8 / RB 5.5;
//   TE1 P4 6.9, G6 5.7. Every row here is a starter (the CB2 is the second starting corner), so P4 6.8 and G6 5.6
//   put a starting corner or safety level with a starting receiver or back. Stored OVRs, raw for those files:
//   QB 77 / 82 / 91 / 98 (13 at 95+), WR 77 / 82 / 89 / 99 (4), RB 78 / 83 / 89 / 93 (0).
//
// ── How a grade is made (scripts/cfb/build-dbs.mjs) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 1. Stats: 2026 to date (weight 1.0 a game), 2025 (0.6) and 2024 (0.35), FBS games only, from ESPN's box scores; games
//    from ESPN's season feed; forced fumbles from the feed.
// 2. Rates a game (INT, PD, INT + PD, tackles, TFL, forced fumbles), INT share of his plays on the ball, solo share of
//    his tackles and yards an INT return, each regressed toward his position's pool rate (4 games of it; 3 INTs for the
//    shares, 20 tackles for solo share), then a z-score among every roster back at his subpos (cb or s) with 4+ weighted
//    FBS games. Role = his share of his team's 2026 games; experience = log(1 + FBS games 2024-26).
// 3. Each trait's evidence is a weighted mix of those z-scores (below), re-standardized so every trait has the same spread.
// 4. HIS LEVEL (the TE file's step): how much he produces at his position.
//      corners:  plays on the ball a game .3, PD a game .2, INT a game .15, role .15, tackles .05, experience .15
//      safeties: tackles .25, INT .25, plays on the ball .2, role .15, experience .15
//    + 0.25 x the z of his 2026 opponents' average FPI offensive efficiency (FCS = 12): the mirror of the offense pools'
//      step 4, so picks and breakups against SEC and Big Ten passing games count for more than the same line in the MAC
//    + 0.25 for a Power 4 schedule (Notre Dame included), -0.2 otherwise (the TE file's step)
//    then small samples shrink toward a prior by slot: level = n/(n+5) x level + 5/(n+5) x prior (n = weighted games;
//    prior CB1 +0.2, CB2 -0.1, S1 +0.2), and the curve is centered on starters (-0.42 corners, -0.6 safeties: the pool
//    counts backups).
//    A trait is 0.62 x his level + 0.5 x n/(n+5) x (that trait's evidence minus the average of his traits' evidence):
//    the level decides how good he is, the evidence what he is good at.
// 5. grade = 5.7 + 1.05 x 2.0 x z (x 0.85 below average) + 0.6 x max(0, z - 1)^2, rounded, 0-11; 11 (S) needs z >= 2.7.
// 6. Size is physical, from ESPN height/weight, on the NFL file's own formula (data/dbs.js dbSizeGrade), against his spot:
//    a corner 175 lb / 69 in = 0, 210 lb / 75 in = 11 (70% weight); a safety 185 lb = 0, 218 lb = 11 (80% weight).
// ovr: the game's own formula (utils/simulation.js calcOVRDB, DB_ATTR_WEIGHT) through the college curve (utils/cfbOvr.js
//    collegeOVR), the number cfbLoad works out from the traits.
//
// Trait evidence (z-scores; "-" = lower is better). The box score can't see targets, coverage snaps or catches allowed,
// so the coverage traits read plays on the ball and role, and the hand-check below brings in what it can't see:
//   hands (Ball Skills): INT .45, INT + PD .35, INT share .2
//   manCoverage: PD .45, INT .2, role .35          press: PD .35, INT .15, role .3, weight .1, height .1
//   zoneIQ: corners INT .4, PD .3, experience .3; safeties INT .5, PD .3, experience .2
//   runSupport: tackles .5, solo share .25, TFL .25          playRecognition: INT .3, TFL .25, forced fumbles .15, experience .3
//   fluidity: role .4, PD .3, -weight .3          speed: role .35, -weight .25, INT return yards .15, PD .25
//   (speed and fluidity: verified 40, track or GPS times replace the frame where found; few were public, see below)
//
// ── The hand-check (2026-11-25) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Sources: the Paycom Jim Thorpe Award semifinalists (Oct. 27) and finalists (Nov. 24: Hampton, McDonald, Moore); the AP,
// CBS, On3 and SI midseason All-America teams; the AP and Walter Camp preseason All-America teams; preseason all-conference
// teams (Sun Belt, Pac-12/MWC Phil Steele, MAC, C-USA Athlon); 2027 boards: Kiper (ESPN, mid-November), PFF's early
// position rankings and top 150, Brugler's top 50 (The Athletic), PFN's position top 10s, Bleacher Report; PFF's top-10
// returning corners and safeties, PFF weekly grade leaders and PFF figures quoted in public articles. Daniel Jeremiah has
// no 2027 top 50 yet. Nothing from Wikipedia. PFF's 2026 season grades are behind its paywall; the quoted ones are used.
// Every Power 4 CB1/S1 and Group of 6 top-40 name was searched against these lists; the moves:
{{HAND}}
//
// ── Top 15 by OVR ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
{{TOP}}
//
// ── Headshots (ESPN only) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// {{HEADSHOTS}} rows have a photo on disk. scripts/fetch-cfb-assets.mjs reads this file (ESPN's college-football photo,
// 350x254 crop, webp q75, public/headshots/cfb_{id}.webp); run it, then re-run this build to fill headshot and skin.
// The rest show initials.
